content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 82.31) are common, suggesting model fails to account for volatility decay.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reverts.
- Forecast horizon bias: 30-day forecasts are too optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually converge but still lag behind true values.
- Model under-reacts to recent low prices — fails to adjust downward when recent history shows downward momentum.
- High volatility spikes in true data are not fully captured by model, leading to underestimation of peak volatility.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term fluctuations, leading to lagged responses to news or policy changes.
